name: Finding Our Place in Time and Space
description: Sundials, astrolabes, chronometers and satellites: the instruments by which sailors and clockmakers learned where and when they were.

checkpoints.name: Shadows and water
checkpoints.note: Sundials and water clocks divided the day, and Greek and Islamic scholars built astrolabes and geared machines like the Antikythera mechanism to model the sky.

checkpoints.name: Compass and chart
checkpoints.note: The compass came from China and portolan charts guided Mediterranean pilots. Sailors used hourglasses and the Jacob’s staff, and the first mechanical clocks rang in towns.

checkpoints.name: The longitude problem
checkpoints.note: Pendulum clocks, the sextant and John Harrison’s marine chronometer helped ships find longitude after disasters at sea, and gave navigators a way to know their place east and west.

checkpoints.name: Electric time and radio waves
checkpoints.note: Wristwatches, gyrocompasses and quartz clocks made time and direction easy to carry. Radar and LORAN used radio waves to find ships and aircraft through night and fog.

checkpoints.name: The satellite age
checkpoints.note: Atomic clocks keep time to a tiny fraction of a second, and the Global Positioning System turned that precision into a map in every pocket.
